Over the next 20 to 50 years, as Western countries become more efficient with AI, robots, and technology, I believe they may have less need for migrant labour. With voices like Tommy Robinson and others continuing to spread anti-immigration messages, moving abroad could become increasingly difficult for the ordinary person.

And even when the opportunity exists, poverty may put it out of reach.

When I moved to the UK, you could make the trip with about $10,000 or even less. Today, depending on the route, you could need ₦30 million to ₦40 million. How many ordinary Nigerians can afford that?

This is why I really want Nigeria and Africa to work. One day, relocating to some of these countries may become almost impossible for the average person. Even those already abroad may reach a point where they would rather return home than continue living there.

We need to build countries where we can live, work, raise our children, and grow without feeling that leaving is our only chance at a better life.
